## Welcome

My work asks a fairly narrow question with wide consequences: when a welfare programme is judged to be working, who decided what "working" means?

I came to this through my master's dissertation, which evaluated India's PM-KISAN direct benefit transfer scheme and found that the administrative metrics used to track delivery obscured targeting failures affecting rural households the programme was built to reach. Since then I have worked on the other side of the same problem — drafting policy briefs for a member of the Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Assembly on service delivery and migration governance in a conflict-affected region, and co-designing groundwater and soil monitoring systems with village residents whose recommendations were taken up at block development level.

I am joining UCL in September 2026 as a Commonwealth Scholar to read for an MSc in Public Policy. Before that I hold a Gold Medal MA in Political Science from Acharya Nagarjuna University, where I graduated top of my cohort, and I currently hold a Junior Research Fellowship from India's Ministry of Education.

On this site you can read more [about my background](about.qmd), the [research I am doing now](research.qmd), and [what I have written](writing.qmd).

I am always glad to hear from people working on state capacity, targeting, or participatory governance — particularly if you are doing fieldwork in India and need a researcher who speaks Telugu and Hindi. You can reach me at [williamkery786@gmail.com](mailto:williamkery786@gmail.com).
